domain_restrictions: m is an integer and m is at least 1
Each entry t_i is either plus 1 or minus 1
If m equals 1, t is the empty sequence
b is a permutation of 1 through m, so its entries are distinct and each lies in 1 through m
The inequality t_i times the difference b_{i+1} minus b_i greater than 0 is required for every i from 1 to m minus 1
semantic_sketch_json.normalized_claim: For every integer m at least 1 and every sign sequence t of length m minus 1 with entries plus 1 or minus 1, the number of permutations b of 1 through m such that t_i times the difference b_{i+1} minus b_i is positive for every i from 1 to m minus 1 is unchanged when every sign in t is flipped. Equivalently, F(t) equals F(-t). In particular, the same holds for the alternating sequence starting with plus 1 and its negation.
quantifier_order: For every integer m at least 1
For every sign sequence t of length m minus 1 with each entry plus 1 or minus 1
For every permutation b of 1 through m, define admissibility by requiring t_i times the difference b_{i+1} minus b_i to be positive for every index i from 1 to m minus 1
F(t) is the number of admissible permutations b
The theorem asserts that F(t) equals F(-t) for all admissible m and t
In particular, the same equality holds for Alt_m^+ and Alt_m^-

The definition of F(t) depends on the full permutation b and requires one inequality for each adjacent index i

statement_nl: Let m be an integer with m at least 1, and let t=(t_1,...,t_{m-1}) be a sign sequence with each t_i equal to plus 1 or minus 1; when m=1, t is the empty sequence. Let F(t) be the number of permutations b=(b_1,...,b_m) of {1,...,m} such that t_i(b_{i+1}-b_i) > 0 for every i=1,...,m-1. Let -t denote the sign sequence (-t_1,...,-t_{m-1}). Then F(t)=F(-t). In particular, if Alt_m^+ is the alternating sign sequence plus 1, minus 1, plus 1, minus 1, ... and Alt_m^- = -Alt_m^+, then F(Alt_m^+)=F(Alt_m^-).
